THE BUSINESS QUESTION

On time. But how well?

A five-workday refund deadline answers only part of the question. This project looks at how quickly customers hear back, whether cases need rework, and what customers say afterward.

01 / METHOD

Follow the whole customer journey.

Receipt → first reply → verification → refund → feedback.

Separate the employee’s verification stage from the accounting stage. Measure elapsed customer waiting time alongside working-time metrics, so nights and weekends do not distort the employee review.

Review speed, quality and feedback together. A low score prompts a closer look at the evidence; it does not automatically assign fault.

02 / LIVE FINDINGS

Evidence for a thoughtful review.

The figures respond to changes in the spreadsheet. All records, ratings and feedback are fictional.

A YEAR IN VIEW

Initial replies within target

Share of cases received in each month. The reply target is editable in the workbook.

THE DECISION THIS SUPPORTS

Recognise good service.
Read the exceptions.

The report gives a manager evidence for the customer-service component of a year-end bonus review. It does not calculate a bonus amount, rank employees, or measure attendance.

SCOPE & ASSUMPTIONS

One complaint type: the account was debited, but the ATM did not dispense cash after a pending/timeout transaction. The baseline contains ten cases per month; eight same-day refunds and two next-workday refunds.

Workdays are Monday–Friday, excluding the holidays listed in Guide. Model hours are 08:00–17:00, with no lunch break. The 30-working-minute reply target is illustrative. A receipt day counts as day zero for the five-workday SLA.

TRY AN EXPERIMENT

One small edit. A visible result.

Reply target: open Guide and change B6 from 30 to 29. Some responses should move outside the target.

Missing feedback: give a blank CSAT cell a score of 1. Survey coverage and low-rating counts should increase; responsibility stays unchanged.

Refund deadline: move a refund beyond its SLA deadline, keeping it on a valid workday. The on-time refund rate should fall.

Inputs support this case study’s 2025 calendar and working-hours model. Invalid values are rejected with an explanation. Formula cells are protected from accidental editing. Downloaded edits keep the workbook’s formulas and current results; the web export uses a simple table layout.
